italian-reading-3.title: C and CH
italian-reading-3.subtitle: Hear the difference between C and CH
italian-reading-3.description: Distinguish soft C in ce/ci from hard C in che/chi.

ir3-p1.translations: Nina has dinner with her friends. Afterward, she goes to the cinema.

ir3-t1.text: ce and ci have the soft C sound: cena, cinema.

ir3-t2.text: In che and chi, H keeps the hard C sound; H itself is not pronounced.

ir3-t3.text: Listen and repeat; do not rely on approximating the sounds with spellings from another language.

ir3_q1.question: Which combinations have the soft C sound?

ir3_q2.question: What does H do in che and chi?

options.ir3_q2_opt1: Keeps the hard C sound before E and I
options.ir3_q2_opt2: Creates a separate sound after C
options.ir3_q2_opt3: Changes C to the soft sound

ir3_q3.question: In which word does C have the soft sound?

ir3_q4.question: Which spelling has hard C before I?

ir3_q5.question: How do you spell the syllable with hard C before I?
